chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who kissed his wife while he was in Ihram. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is a camel (or sacrificial animal), and even if he did not discharge semen, it is not for him to eat from it.'

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْتِ: The Ahl al-Bayt (People of the House), often referring to the Imams
key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: A sacrificial animal (typically a camel, cow, or sheep) offered as expiation
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of Ihram, a ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for kissing one's wife while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the specific expiation (kaffarah) for a man in Ihram who kisses his wife, mandating a camel (badanah) regardless of ejaculation, a ruling that underscores the severity of violating the sanctity of the pilgrimage state. Notably, the prohibition on consuming the sacrificial animal distinguishes this penalty from other expiations, reflecting the unique status of the Ihram restrictions in Shia fiqh. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of the Kufan scholarly network in preserving these precise legal details.
